tasks.taskText: Mime.getType(path) (src/Mime.ts) derives a type from the extension after the last dot of the last path segment. The two regular expressions that strip the directory part and the part before the extension do not match across line terminators, so a file name that contains one is typed wrongly: getType('LINE\nFEED.png') returns null instead of 'image/png', and the same happens for a carriage return (U+000D), a line separator (U+2028) and a paragraph separator (U+2029), with or without a directory part in front. This matters where the file name comes from an untrusted source: a content type decided from it must come from the extension after the last dot of the last segment, whatever characters precede it, so that a name crafted with a line terminator cannot make the lookup fail or pick an earlier extension. Make getType treat every line terminator like any other character when it strips the directory part and the extension's prefix; a space or tab in the name already works and must keep working. getExtension, define and the rest of the class stay as they are. The change belongs in src/Mime.ts only. Repository rules: keep the file's existing style, no new dependencies, no edits under test or types, and the whole suite (npm test, which builds first) must keep passing.

The streaming decoder class Inflate (src/inflate.ts) tracks whether the compressed stream has ended in a private `ended` field, and its push(data, flush_mode) method returns a blanket false for every call made after that point. A compressed stream can end before the caller's data does (trailing bytes after the deflate or gzip stream), and the caller has no way to know that in advance, so a push made after the end must become a no-op that reports the recorded outcome instead: once the stream has ended, push returns true if the decode finished without error (this.err is Z_OK) and false if it failed, whatever data or flush mode it is given, and it leaves `err`, `msg` and `result` exactly as they were, so the delivered result survives any trailing chunks and a failed stream keeps reporting failure. Make `ended` a public, documented property so callers can check it, and document the new push behaviour in its JSDoc. Pushes before the end, the onData and onEnd callbacks, the one-shot inflate helpers and everything else are unchanged. The project's full check (npm test: lint, build, type-check and the node test suite) must keep passing; change only src/inflate.ts (a CHANGELOG entry is welcome but not required) and do not edit tests or benchmarks.
